questions.stem: Gautama Buddha was born at Lumbini in which year (Buddhist tradition)?
questions.explanation: Buddhist tradition places Buddha's birth at 623 BCE at Lumbini (in present-day Nepal) — commemorated internationally as 'Vaishakha Purnima' or Buddha Purnima. Scholarly estimates vary (some say 563 BCE based on other dating methods). 483 BCE is typically cited as his year of MAHAPARINIRVANA (death) at Kushinagar. The NCERT textbook variant often uses 563 BCE; ISI/ASI and Buddhist sources use 623 BCE.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Where did Gautama Buddha attain enlightenment (Bodhi)?
questions.explanation: The Buddha attained enlightenment at BODH GAYA (Bihar) under the Bodhi Tree (a Peepal/Ficus religiosa) at age 35, after 49 days of meditation. Lumbini (Nepal) = birth. Sarnath (UP, near Varanasi) = first sermon ('Dharmachakra Pravartana'). Kushinagar (UP) = death/Mahaparinirvana. These FOUR sites are the main Buddhist pilgrimage circuit ('Char Dham' of Buddhism).
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Buddha delivered his first sermon at Sarnath. In Buddhist terminology, this event is called:
questions.explanation: DHARMACHAKRA PRAVARTANA = 'Setting the Wheel of Dharma in Motion'. The Buddha's first sermon at the Deer Park (Sarnath) outlined the Four Noble Truths to 5 disciples. PRAVRAJYA = act of going forth (renouncing household life). SAMBODHI/BODHI = enlightenment at Bodh Gaya. MAHAPARINIRVANA = final death at Kushinagar. The Dhamek Stupa at Sarnath marks this event.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the Four Noble Truths?

options.option_text: Samudaya — cause of suffering is craving (tanha)
Karma — one reaps what one sows
Nirodha — cessation of suffering is possible

questions.explanation: The FOUR NOBLE TRUTHS (Arya-satyas) are: (1) DUKKHA — suffering exists; (2) SAMUDAYA — cause is craving/tanha; (3) NIRODHA — cessation is possible by extinguishing craving; (4) MAGGA/Marga — the Eightfold Path leads to cessation. KARMA is a general Indian concept of moral causation shared with Hinduism/Jainism, NOT a Noble Truth itself. The Eightfold Path (Magga) has 8 components: right view, intention, speech, action, livelihood, effort, mindfulness, concentration.

questions.stem: The Third Buddhist Council was held during the reign of which emperor?
questions.explanation: FOUR Buddhist Councils: (1) First — 483 BCE at Rajgriha under Ajatashatru, presided by Mahakassapa; (2) Second — 383 BCE at Vaishali under Kalashoka; (3) THIRD — 250 BCE at Pataliputra under ASHOKA, presided by Moggaliputta Tissa (led to codification of Tripitaka and Buddhist missions abroad); (4) Fourth — ~72 CE at Kundalvana (Kashmir) under Kanishka, marked the Mahayana-Hinayana split. Fifth council (19th c.) and Sixth (1954 Yangon) are modern.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Which of the following are the 'Three Jewels' (Triratna) of Buddhism?
questions.explanation: The Triratna (Three Jewels / Three Refuges) of Buddhism are: (1) BUDDHA — the enlightened one; (2) DHAMMA/DHARMA — his teachings; (3) SANGHA — the community of monks and nuns. A Buddhist is formally one who takes refuge in all three: 'Buddham saranam gacchami, Dhammam saranam gacchami, Sangham saranam gacchami'. Ashoka adopted this formula in many of his rock edicts.

questions.stem: Which Buddhist school believed in the Bodhisattva ideal and the worship of Buddha as a deity, and spread to China, Japan, and Korea?
questions.explanation: MAHAYANA ('Greater Vehicle'), which emerged in the 1st c. CE (crystallized at Kanishka's 4th Council), emphasises the Bodhisattva ideal (compassionate enlightened beings postponing own Nirvana to save others) and treats Buddha as divine. Spread to China, Japan, Korea, Vietnam. THERAVADA (formerly 'Hinayana') is older, more conservative, treats Buddha as a human teacher, uses Pali canon — widespread in Sri Lanka, Thailand, Myanmar. VAJRAYANA (Tibetan/Tantric) is a sub-school of Mahayana. ZEN is a Japanese Mahayana school.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The 'Tripitaka' — the scriptural canon of Buddhism — consists of three 'baskets'. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
questions.explanation: The TRIPITAKA (Pali: Tipitaka) has THREE 'baskets': (1) VINAYA PITAKA — monastic discipline and rules for monks/nuns; (2) SUTTA PITAKA — the Buddha's discourses; (3) ABHIDHAMMA PITAKA — systematic philosophical/psychological analysis. 'Avadana' literature (biographical stories of past lives) DOES exist in Buddhist texts but it is part of the Sutta Pitaka's Khuddaka Nikaya — NOT a separate pitaka.
